# Component Reference

## Accordion

```tsx
<Accordion type="single" defaultValue="option-1">
  <Accordion.Item value="option-1">
    <Accordion.Header>
      <Accordion.Trigger>
        <Accordion.Title>Option 1</Accordion.Title>
        <Accordion.Icon />
      </Accordion.Trigger>
    </Accordion.Header>
    <Accordion.Content>
      <Accordion.Section>
        <Accordion.Description>The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog</Accordion.Description>
      </Accordion.Section>
    </Accordion.Content>
  </Accordion.Item>
  <Accordion.Item value="option-2">
    <Accordion.Header>
      <Accordion.Trigger>
        <Accordion.Title>Option 2</Accordion.Title>
        <Accordion.Icon />
      </Accordion.Trigger>
    </Accordion.Header>
    <Accordion.Content>
      <Accordion.Section>
        <Accordion.Description>The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog</Accordion.Description>
      </Accordion.Section>
    </Accordion.Content>
  </Accordion.Item>
</Accordion>
```

Use the compound accordion API with `Accordion.Item`, `Accordion.Header`, `Accordion.Trigger`, `Accordion.Content`, `Accordion.Section`, `Accordion.Title`, `Accordion.Icon`, and `Accordion.Description`. `Accordion.Item` requires a `value`, and the root supports `type` (`single` or `multiple`) plus Radix-style controlled/uncontrolled state props like `defaultValue`.

---

## Alert Dialog

```tsx
<AlertDialog>
  <AlertDialog.Trigger asChild>
    <Button>Trigger</Button>
  </AlertDialog.Trigger>
  <AlertDialog.Portal>
    <AlertDialog.Overlay />
    <AlertDialog.Content>
      <AlertDialog.Section>
        <AlertDialog.Title>The quick brown fox</AlertDialog.Title>
        <AlertDialog.Description>
          Alice was beginning to get very tired of sitting by her sister on the bank.
        </AlertDialog.Description>
      </AlertDialog.Section>
      <AlertDialog.Section className="flex-row justify-end">
        <AlertDialog.Cancel>
          <Button className="variant-outline palette-neutral">Cancel</Button>
        </AlertDialog.Cancel>
        <AlertDialog.Action asChild>
          <Button>Confirm</Button>
        </AlertDialog.Action>
      </AlertDialog.Section>
    </AlertDialog.Content>
  </AlertDialog.Portal>
</AlertDialog>
```

Use the compound alert dialog API with `AlertDialog.Trigger`, `AlertDialog.Portal`, `AlertDialog.Overlay`, `AlertDialog.Content`, `AlertDialog.Section`, `AlertDialog.Title`, `AlertDialog.Description`, `AlertDialog.Cancel`, and `AlertDialog.Action`. `AlertDialog.Trigger` typically renders as a button via `asChild`, and `AlertDialog.Action`/`Cancel` are used for destructive or secondary actions inside the dialog.

---

## App Layout

```tsx
<AppLayout className="min-h-80 text-sm">
  <AppLayout.Header>Header</AppLayout.Header>
  <AppLayout.Body>
    <AppLayout.Sidenav>Sidenav</AppLayout.Sidenav>
    <AppLayout.Main>
      <AppLayout.Section>Main</AppLayout.Section>
    </AppLayout.Main>
    <AppLayout.Aside>Aside</AppLayout.Aside>
  </AppLayout.Body>
  <AppLayout.Footer>Footer</AppLayout.Footer>
</AppLayout>
```

Use `AppLayout` as a semantic page shell composed of `Header`, `Body`, `Sidenav`, `Main`, `Aside`, `Footer`, and optional `Section` blocks. It is primarily used for dashboard and document-style layouts rather than ordinary page containers.

---

## Avatar

```tsx
<Avatar>
  <Avatar.Image src="/images/assets/avatar-0.webp" alt="avatar" />
</Avatar>
```

Use the compound avatar API with `Avatar.Image` and `Avatar.Fallback`. The image is the primary visual, and `Avatar.Fallback` is used as a text fallback when the image is unavailable or still loading. Keep `alt` text meaningful and concise.

---

## Badge

```tsx
<Badge>Badge</Badge>
```

Use `Badge` for compact status, labels, or metadata. It accepts normal children and can contain inline icon content. Prefer concise text and reuse the library’s sizing/variant utilities rather than custom styling.

---

## Bg Image

```tsx
<Box className="relative overflow-hidden">
  <BgImage src="/images/assets/espresso.webp" className="brightness-50" />
  <Center>
    <Description className="text-xl text-white drop-shadow-md">
      The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog
    </Description>
  </Center>
</Box>
```

Use `BgImage` as a background media layer with a `src` prop, typically paired with `Overlay` and text content inside a containing layout. It is meant for decorative hero or panel backgrounds, not for standard image rendering.

---

## Blockquote

```tsx
<Blockquote>
  <Blockquote.Icon />
  <Blockquote.Content>
    <Blockquote.Description>Good design is as little design as possible.</Blockquote.Description>
    <Blockquote.Caption>
      <Blockquote.Cite>— Dieter Rams</Blockquote.Cite>
    </Blockquote.Caption>
  </Blockquote.Content>
</Blockquote>
```

Use the compound blockquote API with `Blockquote.Icon`, `Blockquote.Content`, `Blockquote.Description`, `Blockquote.Caption`, and `Blockquote.Cite`. It is intended for quoted editorial or testimonial content, typically paired with a leading accent or icon treatment.

---

## Box

```tsx
<Box>Box</Box>
```

`Box` is the base layout primitive for generic wrapping content. Use it for spacing, borders, backgrounds, and simple structural containers without introducing custom styling when a utility class or variant already covers the need.

---

## Breadcrumbs

```tsx
<Breadcrumbs>
  <Breadcrumbs.List>
    <Breadcrumbs.Item>
      <Breadcrumbs.Link href="#">Home</Breadcrumbs.Link>
    </Breadcrumbs.Item>
    <Breadcrumbs.Separator />
    <Breadcrumbs.Item>
      <Breadcrumbs.Link href="#">Profile</Breadcrumbs.Link>
    </Breadcrumbs.Item>
    <Breadcrumbs.Separator />
    <Breadcrumbs.Item>
      <Breadcrumbs.CurrentLink href="#">Settings</Breadcrumbs.CurrentLink>
    </Breadcrumbs.Item>
  </Breadcrumbs.List>
</Breadcrumbs>
```

Use `Breadcrumbs` for hierarchical navigation with `List`, `Item`, `Link`, `CurrentLink`, and `Separator`. Keep labels short and maintain semantic navigation structure for accessibility.

---

## Button

```tsx
<Button>Button</Button>
```

`Button` is the primary action component. Use the library’s sizing and variant utilities (`size-*`, `variant-*`, `palette-*`) for consistent styling, and include icons only when they add clear meaning to the action.

---

## Card

```tsx
<Card>
  <Card.Content>
    <Card.Section>
      <Card.Title>Header</Card.Title>
      <Card.Description>
        Alice was beginning to get very tired of sitting by her sister on the bank.
      </Card.Description>
    </Card.Section>
  </Card.Content>
</Card>
```

Use `Card` for grouped content blocks with `Card.Content`, `Card.Section`, `Card.Title`, and `Card.Description`. It is ideal for media-rich panels, summaries, and action surfaces that should remain visually cohesive.

---

## Center

```tsx
<Center>The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog</Center>
```

```tsx
<Box className="relative">
  <AbsoluteCenter>The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog</AbsoluteCenter>
</Box>
```

Use `Center` to horizontally and vertically center a single child within its parent. For positioning inside a relative container, prefer `AbsoluteCenter` when you want the item centered by absolute positioning rather than normal layout flow.

---

## Checkbox

```tsx
<Checkbox>
  <Checkbox.Control id="ch1" aria-label="Accept terms" defaultChecked>
    <Checkbox.Indicator />
  </Checkbox.Control>
  <Checkbox.Label htmlFor="ch1">Accept terms</Checkbox.Label>
</Checkbox>
```

Use the compound checkbox API with `Checkbox.Control`, `Checkbox.Indicator`, and `Checkbox.Label`. For a controlled checkbox, pass `checked` and `onCheckedChange`; for an uncontrolled checkbox, use `defaultChecked` or a form `name` value.

---

## CheckboxCard

```tsx
<CheckboxCard>
  <CheckboxCard.Indicator />
  <CheckboxCard.Content>
    <CheckboxCard.Label>Accept Terms</CheckboxCard.Label>
    <CheckboxCard.Description>Agree to all terms and conditions</CheckboxCard.Description>
  </CheckboxCard.Content>
</CheckboxCard>
```

Use `CheckboxCard` for selectable list items or form choices that need a larger, card-style interaction surface. Keep the label and description concise and pair it with `CheckboxCard.Indicator` and a single `CheckboxCard.Content` block.

---

## CloseButton

```tsx
<CloseButton aria-label="Close" />
```

`CloseButton` is a compact dismiss control for dialogs, drawers, or notification surfaces. Always provide an accessible `aria-label` because it is an icon-only control.

---

## Code

```tsx
<Code>console.log()</Code>
```

Use `Code` for inline or block-level code snippets. Prefer the library’s text sizing and mono styling utilities to maintain consistency across examples, command lines, and small code fragments.

---

## Collapsible

```tsx
<Collapsible>
  <Collapsible.Trigger asChild>
    <Button>Trigger</Button>
  </Collapsible.Trigger>
  <Collapsible.Content>The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog</Collapsible.Content>
</Collapsible>
```

Use `Collapsible.Trigger` to toggle `Collapsible.Content`. When the trigger is a library button or another existing interactive element, use `asChild` so the component preserves the intended accessible control.

---

## Color Swatch

```tsx
<ColorSwatch />
```

Use `ColorSwatch` for a compact color indicator. Apply the documented size and variant utilities when the swatch needs to match a particular control or palette.

---

## Container

```tsx
<Container>Content</Container>
```

Use `Container` to constrain content to the component's responsive maximum width.

---

## Context Menu

```tsx
<ContextMenu>
  <ContextMenu.Trigger asChild>
    <IconButton aria-label="Open context menu">
      <LuMenu />
    </IconButton>
  </ContextMenu.Trigger>
  <ContextMenu.Portal>
    <ContextMenu.Content>
      <ContextMenu.Section>
        <ContextMenu.Item>
          <ContextMenu.Indicator>
            <LuTextSelect />
          </ContextMenu.Indicator>
          Select All
          <ContextMenu.Command>Ctrl+A</ContextMenu.Command>
        </ContextMenu.Item>
        <ContextMenu.Separator />
        <ContextMenu.Label>Actions</ContextMenu.Label>
        <ContextMenu.Item>New Tab</ContextMenu.Item>
      </ContextMenu.Section>
    </ContextMenu.Content>
  </ContextMenu.Portal>
</ContextMenu>
```

Use the compound context menu API with `Trigger`, `Portal`, `Content`, `Section`, `Item`, `Indicator`, `Command`, `Separator`, and `Label`. Keep the trigger keyboard accessible and use `CheckboxItem`, `RadioGroup`, or `Sub` for the corresponding menu behaviors.

---

## Design Grid

```tsx
<Box className="palette-neutral variant-subtle relative h-40 w-full">
  <DesignGrid className="absolute grid-cols-8 grid-rows-4" />
</Box>
```

`DesignGrid` is a visual layout aid. It uses a fixed position by default, so specify `grid-cols-*` and/or `grid-rows-*` and place it inside a positioned parent when that parent should contain the grid.

---

## Dialog

```tsx
<Dialog>
  <Dialog.Trigger asChild>
    <Button>Open</Button>
  </Dialog.Trigger>
  <Dialog.Portal>
    <Dialog.Overlay />
    <Dialog.Content>
      <Dialog.Section>
        <Dialog.Title>Title</Dialog.Title>
        <Dialog.Description>Description</Dialog.Description>
      </Dialog.Section>
      <Dialog.Close aria-label="Close" />
    </Dialog.Content>
  </Dialog.Portal>
</Dialog>
```

Use the compound dialog API with `Trigger`, `Portal`, `Overlay`, `Content`, `Section`, `Title`, `Description`, and `Close`. Put the overlay and content inside the portal, and give icon-only close controls an accessible label.

---

## Drawer

```tsx
<Drawer>
  <Drawer.Trigger asChild>
    <Button>Open</Button>
  </Drawer.Trigger>
  <Drawer.Portal>
    <Drawer.Overlay />
    <Drawer.Content>
      <Drawer.Section>
        <Drawer.Title>Title</Drawer.Title>
        <Drawer.Description>Description</Drawer.Description>
      </Drawer.Section>
      <Drawer.Close aria-label="Close" />
    </Drawer.Content>
  </Drawer.Portal>
</Drawer>
```

Use the compound drawer API with `Trigger`, `Portal`, `Overlay`, `Content`, `Section`, `Title`, `Description`, and `Close`. Set `placement` on `Drawer.Content` when the panel should open from `start`, `end`, `top`, or `bottom`.

---

## Dropdown Menu

```tsx
<DropdownMenu>
  <DropdownMenu.Trigger asChild>
    <IconButton aria-label="Open dropdown menu">
      <LuMenu />
    </IconButton>
  </DropdownMenu.Trigger>
  <DropdownMenu.Portal>
    <DropdownMenu.Content>
      <DropdownMenu.Section>
        <DropdownMenu.Item>
          <DropdownMenu.Indicator>
            <LuTextSelect />
          </DropdownMenu.Indicator>
          Select All
          <DropdownMenu.Command>Ctrl+A</DropdownMenu.Command>
        </DropdownMenu.Item>
        <DropdownMenu.Separator />
        <DropdownMenu.Label>Actions</DropdownMenu.Label>
        <DropdownMenu.Item>New Tab</DropdownMenu.Item>
      </DropdownMenu.Section>
      <DropdownMenu.Arrow />
    </DropdownMenu.Content>
  </DropdownMenu.Portal>
</DropdownMenu>
```

Use the compound dropdown menu API with `Trigger`, `Portal`, `Content`, `Section`, `Item`, `Indicator`, `Command`, `Separator`, `Label`, and optional `Arrow`. Use `CheckboxItem`, `RadioGroup`, and `Sub` for menus that contain selection state or nested actions.

---

## Element

```tsx
<Element as="section" className="p-4">
  Content
</Element>
```

Use `Element` as the low-level polymorphic primitive when a semantic tag must change without adding a wrapper. Use `asChild` only when the child should provide the rendered element, and prefer higher-level extraction-ui components when one already expresses the intended behavior.

---

## Empty State

```tsx
<EmptyState>
  <EmptyState.Content>
    <EmptyState.Section>
      <EmptyState.Indicator>
        <LuMail />
      </EmptyState.Indicator>
      <EmptyState.Title>Header</EmptyState.Title>
      <EmptyState.Description>Alice was beginning to get very tired</EmptyState.Description>
    </EmptyState.Section>
  </EmptyState.Content>
</EmptyState>
```

Use the compound empty state API with `EmptyState.Content`, `EmptyState.Section`, `EmptyState.Indicator`, `EmptyState.Title`, and `EmptyState.Description`. Keep the message specific to the missing content or unavailable result, and use the indicator for a meaningful visual cue.

---

## Field

```tsx
<Field>
  <Field.Label htmlFor="name">
    Name
    <Field.RequiredIndicator />
  </Field.Label>
  <Input>
    <Input.Field id="name" placeholder="Enter your name" />
  </Input>
  <Field.Helper>The quick brown fox jumps over</Field.Helper>
</Field>
```

Use the compound field API with `Field.Label`, `Field.RequiredIndicator`, and helper or validation messaging such as `Field.Helper`, `Field.Success`, and `Field.Error`. Associate the label with the input through `htmlFor` and the input `id`.

---

## Flex

```tsx
<Flex>
  <Box>Item 1</Box>
  <Box>Item 2</Box>
  <Box>Item 3</Box>
</Flex>
```

Use `Flex` for one-dimensional layouts. Its default layout is intended for horizontally arranged children, with spacing controlled by the component styles and utility classes.

---

## Float

```tsx
<Box className="relative">
  <Float>
    <Box />
  </Float>
</Box>
```

Use `Float` to position a child relative to its containing surface. Apply the documented position utilities when the floating element needs a specific corner or edge placement.

---

## Grid

```tsx
<Grid>
  <Box>Item 1</Box>
  <Box>Item 2</Box>
  <Box>Item 3</Box>
</Grid>
```

Use `Grid` for two-dimensional layouts and combine it with grid utility classes for columns, rows, and gaps. Prefer responsive grid utilities when the layout changes at different viewport sizes.

---

## Group

```tsx
<Group>
  <Button>Item 1</Button>
  <Button>Item 2</Button>
  <Button>Item 3</Button>
</Group>
```

Use `Group` to keep related controls visually connected. Pass `orientation="vertical"` when the group should arrange its children vertically.

---

## Highlight

```tsx
<Text>
  The quick brown fox <Highlight>jumps over</Highlight> the lazy dog
</Text>
```

Use `Highlight` to emphasize a short portion of surrounding text. Keep the highlighted content brief and use the component's variants for the visual treatment rather than recreating the highlight with custom markup.

---

## Hover Card

```tsx
<HoverCard>
  <HoverCard.Trigger asChild>
    <Button>Hover me</Button>
  </HoverCard.Trigger>
  <HoverCard.Portal>
    <HoverCard.Content>
      <HoverCard.Section>
        <HoverCard.Title>The quick brown fox</HoverCard.Title>
        <HoverCard.Description>
          Alice was beginning to get very tired of sitting by her sister on the bank.
        </HoverCard.Description>
      </HoverCard.Section>
      <HoverCard.Arrow />
    </HoverCard.Content>
  </HoverCard.Portal>
</HoverCard>
```

Use the compound hover card API with `Trigger`, `Portal`, `Content`, `Section`, `Title`, `Description`, and optional `Arrow`. Set `side` on `HoverCard.Content` to choose `top`, `right`, `bottom`, or `left` placement.

---

## Icon

```tsx
<Icon>
  <LuMail />
</Icon>
```

`Icon` is a styling wrapper and does not provide icons itself. Use an icon from the project's chosen icon library or a custom SVG, and keep icon-only interactive controls labelled with `aria-label`.

---

## Icon Box

```tsx
<IconBox>
  <LuMail />
</IconBox>
```

Use `IconBox` for an icon inside a consistently sized, styled container. Apply the documented sizes and variants when the icon box is used as a visual marker or compact feature indicator.

---

## IconButton

```tsx
<IconButton aria-label="Icon button">
  <LuMail />
</IconButton>
```

Use `IconButton` for actions represented by an icon without visible text. Every icon-only button must have a meaningful `aria-label`, and it supports the documented button sizes and variants.

---

## Image

```tsx
<Image src="/image.jpg" alt="image" />
```

Use `Image` for rendered image content and always provide descriptive `alt` text. Use aspect-ratio utilities such as `aspect-square`, `aspect-video`, or `aspect-auto` when the media needs a stable ratio.

---

## Input

```tsx
<Input>
  <Input.Field placeholder="Enter your name" />
</Input>
```

Use the compound input API with `Input.Field`. For controlled inputs, pass `value` and `onChange` to `Input.Field`; for uncontrolled form fields, provide a `name`. Use `Field` when the input needs an associated label or validation messaging.

---

## KBD

```tsx
<HStack>
  <Kbd>Cmd</Kbd>+<Kbd>Shift</Kbd>+<Kbd>K</Kbd>
</HStack>
```

Use `Kbd` to display keyboard keys or shortcuts. Combine multiple `Kbd` elements with `HStack` when showing a sequence, and use the documented text sizes and variants for presentation.

---

## Link

```tsx
<div>
  The quick <Link href="#">brown fox</Link> jumps over the lazy dog
</div>
```

Use `Link` for navigational text and provide a valid `href`. Keep link text descriptive, and use the documented text-decoration and interaction utilities for its visual states.

---

## List

```tsx
<List>
  <List.Item>First item of the list</List.Item>
  <List.Item>Second item of the list</List.Item>
</List>
```

Use the compound list API with `List.Item`. Add `List.Indicator` when items need custom markers, such as an icon, and use list-style utilities when the native marker treatment is appropriate.

---

## Loader

```tsx
<Loader />
```

Use `Loader` to communicate an in-progress operation. Apply the documented size and palette utilities to match the surrounding interface while preserving the component's loading semantics.

---

## Logo

```tsx
<Logo src="/logo.svg" alt="Logo" />
```

Use `Logo` for brand artwork and always provide meaningful `alt` text. Use the component's sizing utilities or semantic rendering props when the logo needs to fit a different layout context.

---

## Mark

```tsx
<Text>
  The quick brown fox <Mark>jumps over</Mark> the lazy dog
</Text>
```

Use `Mark` to emphasize a short inline text fragment. Keep the marked content concise and use the documented variants for the emphasis style.

---

## Menubar

```tsx
<Menubar>
  <Menubar.Menu>
    <Menubar.Trigger>File</Menubar.Trigger>
    <Menubar.Portal>
      <Menubar.Content>
        <Menubar.Section>
          <Menubar.Item>New Tab</Menubar.Item>
          <Menubar.Separator />
          <Menubar.Label>Actions</Menubar.Label>
          <Menubar.Item>
            Select All
            <Menubar.Command>Cmd+A</Menubar.Command>
          </Menubar.Item>
        </Menubar.Section>
        <Menubar.Arrow />
      </Menubar.Content>
    </Menubar.Portal>
  </Menubar.Menu>
</Menubar>
```

Use the compound menubar API with `Menu`, `Trigger`, `Portal`, `Content`, `Section`, `Item`, `Separator`, `Label`, `Command`, and optional `Arrow`. Use `Sub`, `CheckboxItem`, and `RadioGroup` for nested actions and selection state.

---

## Native Select

```tsx
<NativeSelect>
  <NativeSelect.Field aria-label="Select field">
    <option>Option 1</option>
    <option>Option 2</option>
  </NativeSelect.Field>
  <NativeSelect.Icon />
</NativeSelect>
```

Use the compound native select API with `NativeSelect.Field` and `NativeSelect.Icon`. For controlled usage, pass `value` and `onChange`; for an uncontrolled form field, provide a `name` on `NativeSelect.Field`.

---

## Nav Button

```tsx
<NavButton>
  <LuMail />
  Button
</NavButton>
```

Use `NavButton` for button-like controls within navigation surfaces. It supports the documented sizes and variants and can contain an icon alongside its label.

---

## Nav Link

```tsx
<NavLink>
  <LuMail />
  Nav Link
</NavLink>
```

Use `NavLink` for navigation controls styled as links. Keep the visible label descriptive, and use its documented sizes, variants, and disabled state consistently with the surrounding navigation.

---

## NavigationMenu

```tsx
<NavigationMenu>
  <NavigationMenu.List>
    <NavigationMenu.Item>
      <NavigationMenu.Trigger>Home</NavigationMenu.Trigger>
      <NavigationMenu.Content>
        <NavigationMenu.Section>The quick brown fox</NavigationMenu.Section>
      </NavigationMenu.Content>
    </NavigationMenu.Item>
    <NavigationMenu.Item>
      <NavigationMenu.Link href="/google">Google</NavigationMenu.Link>
    </NavigationMenu.Item>
  </NavigationMenu.List>
  <NavigationMenu.ViewportAnchor>
    <NavigationMenu.Viewport />
  </NavigationMenu.ViewportAnchor>
</NavigationMenu>
```

Use the compound navigation menu API with `List`, `Item`, `Trigger`, `Content`, `Section`, `Link`, `ViewportAnchor`, and `Viewport`. Use `Sub` with a nested `List` and `Viewport` for multi-level navigation, and set `orientation="vertical"` when needed.

## Overlay

```tsx
<Box className="relative">
  <Overlay />
</Box>
```

Use `Overlay` as a visual layer over positioned content. Place it inside a `relative` container and preserve sufficient contrast for any content layered above it.

---

## Password

```tsx
<Password>
  <Password.Input placeholder="Enter your password" />
  <Password.Toggle>
    <Password.Icon />
  </Password.Toggle>
</Password>
```

Use the compound password API with `Password.Input`, `Password.Toggle`, and `Password.Icon`. For controlled usage, pass `value` and `onChange` to `Password.Input`; for an uncontrolled form field, provide its `name`.

---

## Pin Input

```tsx
<PinInput placeholder="○○○">
  <PinInput.Field />
  <PinInput.Field />
  <PinInput.Field />
  <PinInput.Hidden />
</PinInput>
```

Use `PinInput.Field` for each visible character cell and include `PinInput.Hidden` for the aggregate form value. Use `value` and `onValueChange` for controlled usage, `name` for uncontrolled form submission, and `type="password"` to mask the entered PIN.

---

## Popover

```tsx
<Popover>
  <Popover.Trigger asChild>
    <Button>Click me</Button>
  </Popover.Trigger>
  <Popover.Portal>
    <Popover.Content>
      <Popover.Section>
        <Popover.Title>The quick brown fox</Popover.Title>
        <Popover.Description>
          Alice was beginning to get very tired of sitting by her sister on the bank.
        </Popover.Description>
      </Popover.Section>
      <Popover.Close aria-label="Close" />
      <Popover.Arrow />
    </Popover.Content>
  </Popover.Portal>
</Popover>
```

Use the compound popover API with `Trigger`, `Portal`, `Content`, `Section`, `Title`, `Description`, `Close`, and optional `Arrow`. Set `side` on `Popover.Content` to choose `top`, `right`, `bottom`, or `left` placement.

---

## Progress

```tsx
<Progress aria-label="Progress">
  <Progress.Indicator className="max-w-[50%]" />
</Progress>
```

Use `Progress.Indicator` to show the current progress within `Progress`. Provide an accessible label and set `orientation="vertical"` with a corresponding height-constrained indicator when the progress bar is vertical.

---

## Radio

```tsx
<RadioGroup defaultValue="option-1">
  <Radio>
    <Radio.Control value="option-1" id="r1">
      <Radio.Indicator />
    </Radio.Control>
    <Radio.Label htmlFor="r1">Option 1</Radio.Label>
  </Radio>
  <Radio>
    <Radio.Control value="option-2" id="r2">
      <Radio.Indicator />
    </Radio.Control>
    <Radio.Label htmlFor="r2">Option 2</Radio.Label>
  </Radio>
</RadioGroup>
```

Use the compound radio API with `RadioGroup`, `Radio.Control`, `Radio.Indicator`, and `Radio.Label`. Associate each label with its control through `htmlFor` and `id`; use `value` and `onValueChange` for controlled groups.

---

## Radio Card

```tsx
<RadioGroup defaultValue="option-1">
  <RadioCard value="option-1">
    <RadioCard.Indicator />
    <RadioCard.Content>
      <RadioCard.Label>Option 1</RadioCard.Label>
    </RadioCard.Content>
  </RadioCard>
  <RadioCard value="option-2">
    <RadioCard.Indicator />
    <RadioCard.Content>
      <RadioCard.Label>Option 2</RadioCard.Label>
    </RadioCard.Content>
  </RadioCard>
</RadioGroup>
```

Use `RadioCard` inside `RadioGroup` for larger selectable options. Each card requires a unique `value` and is composed from `Indicator`, `Content`, and `Label`.

---

## Radio Group

```tsx
<RadioGroup defaultValue="option-1" name="radio">
  <Radio>...</Radio>
  <Radio>...</Radio>
</RadioGroup>
```

Use `RadioGroup` to manage a mutually exclusive set of `Radio` or `RadioCard` choices. Use `defaultValue` for uncontrolled state, `value` with `onValueChange` for controlled state, and `name` when the group participates in form submission.

---

## Scroll Area

```tsx
<ScrollArea className="h-80">
  <ScrollArea.Viewport tabIndex={0}>
    <ScrollArea.Content>
      <Description>Scrollable content</Description>
    </ScrollArea.Content>
  </ScrollArea.Viewport>
  <ScrollArea.Scrollbar orientation="vertical">
    <ScrollArea.Thumb />
  </ScrollArea.Scrollbar>
  <ScrollArea.Scrollbar orientation="horizontal">
    <ScrollArea.Thumb />
  </ScrollArea.Scrollbar>
  <ScrollArea.Corner />
</ScrollArea>
```

Use the compound scroll area API with `Viewport`, `Content`, `Scrollbar`, `Thumb`, and optional `Corner`. Add a horizontal scrollbar when needed, and make the viewport keyboard accessible when it is the scrolling surface.

---

## Section

```tsx
<Section>Content</Section>
```

Use `Section` as a semantic page or content band with the library's responsive vertical spacing. Prefer it over a generic wrapper when the content represents a distinct section of a layout.

---

## Select

```tsx
<Select>
  <Select.Trigger aria-label="Select an option">
    <Select.Value placeholder="Select an option" />
    <Select.Icon />
  </Select.Trigger>
  <Select.Portal>
    <Select.Content>
      <Select.Viewport>
        <Select.Section>
          <Select.Item value="opt-1">
            <Select.ItemText>Option 1</Select.ItemText>
            <Select.ItemIndicator />
          </Select.Item>
          <Select.Item value="opt-2">
            <Select.ItemText>Option 2</Select.ItemText>
            <Select.ItemIndicator />
          </Select.Item>
        </Select.Section>
      </Select.Viewport>
    </Select.Content>
  </Select.Portal>
</Select>
```

Use the compound select API with `Trigger`, `Value`, `Icon`, `Portal`, `Content`, `Viewport`, `Section`, `Item`, `ItemText`, and `ItemIndicator`. Give the trigger an accessible label and use `value`/`onValueChange` for controlled selection.

---

## Separator

```tsx
<Stack>
  <Box>Above</Box>
  <Separator />
  <Box>Below</Box>
</Stack>
```

Use `Separator` to divide related content. Set `orientation="vertical"` when separating horizontally arranged items, and use its optional content and alignment props when the divider includes a label.

---

## Skeleton

```tsx
<Skeleton className="h-20" />
```

Use `Skeleton` for loading placeholders that preserve the shape of the eventual content. Pass `loading` with children when the component should switch between the placeholder and real content.

---

## Slider

```tsx
<Slider defaultValue={[50]}>
  <Slider.Track>
    <Slider.Range />
  </Slider.Track>
  <Slider.Thumb aria-label="Slider thumb" />
</Slider>
```

Use the compound slider API with `Track`, `Range`, and one or more accessible `Thumb` elements. Use `value` and `onValueChange` for controlled state, `defaultValue` for uncontrolled state, and `orientation="vertical"` for vertical sliders.

---

## Stack

```tsx
<Stack>
  <Box>Item 1</Box>
  <Box>Item 2</Box>
</Stack>
```

Use `Stack` for vertically arranged content and pass a component through `separator` when items need visual separation. Use `HStack` for horizontal arrangements and `VStack` for an explicit vertical stack.

---

## Status

```tsx
<Status />
```

Use `Status` as a compact status indicator. Apply the documented sizes and variants to communicate state consistently without replacing the component with an arbitrary decorative element.

---

## Switch

```tsx
<Switch>
  <Switch.Thumb aria-label="Switch" />
</Switch>
```

Use the compound switch API with `Switch.Thumb`. The thumb needs an accessible label when it is the only control text; use `checked` and `onCheckedChange` for controlled state or `name` for uncontrolled form submission.

---

## Table

```tsx
<Table>
  <Table.Head>
    <Table.Row>
      <Table.Header>#</Table.Header>
      <Table.Header>Header</Table.Header>
    </Table.Row>
  </Table.Head>
  <Table.Body>
    <Table.Row>
      <Table.Header>1</Table.Header>
      <Table.Cell>Cell 1</Table.Cell>
    </Table.Row>
  </Table.Body>
</Table>
```

Use the compound table API with `Head`, `Body`, `Row`, `Header`, `Cell`, `Foot`, and optional `Caption`. Keep header cells associated with their columns and use the documented table utilities for striped, bordered, or interactive rows.

---

## Tabs

```tsx
<Tabs defaultValue="tab1">
  <Tabs.List>
    <Tabs.Trigger value="tab1">One</Tabs.Trigger>
    <Tabs.Trigger value="tab2">Two</Tabs.Trigger>
  </Tabs.List>
  <Tabs.Content value="tab1">
    <Box className="box-md">Tab one content</Box>
  </Tabs.Content>
  <Tabs.Content value="tab2">
    <Box className="box-md">Tab two content</Box>
  </Tabs.Content>
</Tabs>
```

Use the compound tabs API with `List`, `Trigger`, and matching `Content` values. Use `value` and `onValueChange` for controlled tabs, and set `orientation="vertical"` when the tab list should run vertically.

---

## Text

```tsx
<Text>The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog</Text>
```

Use `Text` for body and inline copy. Keep semantic structure in mind and use the component's text sizing utilities rather than applying arbitrary typography values.

---

## Textarea

```tsx
<Textarea>
  <Textarea.Field placeholder="Enter your name" />
</Textarea>
```

Use the compound textarea API with `Textarea.Field`. For controlled usage, pass `value` and `onChange` to the field; for uncontrolled form submission, provide a `name`. Wrap it with `Field` when it needs a label or validation message.

---

## Toast

```tsx
const Example = () => {
  const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false);

  return (
    <Toast.Provider>
      <Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Trigger</Button>
      <Toast open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
        <Toast.Indicator />
        <Toast.Content>
          <Toast.Title>The quick brown fox</Toast.Title>
          <Toast.Description>
            Alice was beginning to get very tired of sitting by her sister on the bank.
          </Toast.Description>
        </Toast.Content>
        <Toast.Close aria-label="Close" />
      </Toast>
      <Toast.Viewport />
    </Toast.Provider>;
  );
};

```

Use the compound toast API with `Provider`, `Toast`, `Indicator`, `Content`, `Title`, `Description`, `Close`, and `Viewport`. Control visibility with `open` and `onOpenChange`, and give the icon-only close control an accessible label.

---

## Toggle

```tsx
<Toggle asChild>
  <IconButton aria-label="Toggle mail">
    <LuMail />
  </IconButton>
</Toggle>
```

Use `Toggle` for a two-state pressed/unpressed action. Use `asChild` when composing it with `IconButton`, provide an accessible label, and use `pressed`/`onPressedChange` for controlled state.

---

## Toggle Group

```tsx
<ToggleGroup type="single">
  <Group>
    <ToggleGroup.Item value="item-1" asChild>
      <IconButton aria-label="Align left">
        <LuAlignLeft />
      </IconButton>
    </ToggleGroup.Item>
    <ToggleGroup.Item value="item-2" asChild>
      <IconButton aria-label="Align center">
        <LuAlignCenter />
      </IconButton>
    </ToggleGroup.Item>
  </Group>
</ToggleGroup>
```

Use `ToggleGroup` with `ToggleGroup.Item` for related toggle controls. Set `type="single"` for one selected item or `type="multiple"` for independent selections, and use `value`/`onValueChange` for controlled state.

---

## Tooltip

```tsx
<Tooltip.Provider>
  <Tooltip>
    <Tooltip.Trigger>
      <Button>Hover me</Button>
    </Tooltip.Trigger>
    <Tooltip.Portal>
      <Tooltip.Content>
        The quick brown fox.
        <Tooltip.Arrow />
      </Tooltip.Content>
    </Tooltip.Portal>
  </Tooltip>
</Tooltip.Provider>
```

Use the compound tooltip API with `Tooltip.Provider`, `Tooltip.Trigger`, `Tooltip.Portal`, `Tooltip.Content`, and optional `Tooltip.Arrow`. Set `side` on `Tooltip.Content` to place the tooltip on the `top`, `right`, `bottom`, or `left` side of its trigger.
